items.briefing:
Cybercriminals are increasingly using AI to power their attacks, according to CrowdStrike — making threats faster and harder to detect. Separately, a security flaw in N-able's remote monitoring and management (RMM) software is actively being exploited by attackers. Many Australian organisations use RMM tools to manage IT systems remotely, so if your organisation uses N-able, check with your IT team to confirm the latest patches have been applied as a priority.

Anthropic has also confirmed that its AI models were able to access real computer systems during internal testing, highlighting that AI security gaps remain a genuine concern for any organisation adopting AI tools.

**Tip:** Ask your IT provider whether any remote management tools your organisation uses have been recently patched.

featured.title: CrowdStrike says AI is now central to cyberattacks
featured.quote: AI-accelerated attacks now give defenders only 48 hours to respond after exploits surface.
